notes: The site was found at the published coordinates: protected open ground at about 26.1734 N, 68.3228 E, in two light lobes (south-west and north-east) joined by a neck, between a metalled road on the south-east and fields. Zoom 19 tiles are placeholders here, so the 2025 image is used at z18, and the ring is taken from the 2019-10 Wayback release at z17, where it is clearest; a road crossing and tree clumps compared across releases agree to about 5 m. Plate IV shows only Mound II, so it is chained through Plate I, the contour map of the whole site in the same volume, with 12 grid pegs. Plate I labels its letters on grid lines and its numbers on the strips between lines. Warping Plate I onto Plate IV under each reading of the numbers showed that Plate IV's peg row n is the lower edge of Plate I's strip n: under that reading the Mound II contours of the two plates coincide line for line, and under the other they are one square apart. The lobes were assigned to mounds by size and shape: the south-west lobe is Mound I, and the larger north-east area holds Mound II with Mound III towards its north edge. Exploratory checks and overlays on scratch files outside the control directory tested that assignment: a fit from the four Mound I corners alone placed Plate I's Mound II contours on the bare ground of the north-east area and the Pir's tomb within about 10 m of the ring, which supports both identifications, and the ring was then added. Plate I's 5 ft contour of Mound I runs along the map frame on its south side, so the south corners are taken at the bends of the west and east sides. The plates carry magnetic-north arrows, which were not used. While reading the text for context, Mackay 1943 p. 2 (PDF page index 22) was found to give compass directions for trench lines ('cut in a south-westerly direction' for Trenches A(2) and A(3)); reading of the text stopped there.
